zero_omission_notes.summary: Examines carbon's covalent bonding, tetravalency, and catenation capabilities. Covers homologous series, functional groups, organic reactions (combustion, oxidation, addition, substitution, esterification), and soap micelle mechanics.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Carbon cannot gain 4 e- (C4- unstable due to 6 protons holding 10 e-) nor lose 4 e- (C4+ requires huge ionization energy). Hence, it shares electrons forming strong covalent bonds.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Diamond vs Graphite
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: In diamond, each C bonds to 4 others tetrahedrally (hardest). In graphite, each C bonds to 3 in hexagonal layers with free electrons (conducts electricity).

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: To synthesize an ester from ethanoic acid and ethanol.
procedure_or_steps: Mix ethanol, ethanoic acid, and drops of H2SO4 in test tube.
Warm in water bath for 5 minutes.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: A pleasant, sweet, fruity aroma is produced.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Acid-catalysed reaction between carboxylic acid and alcohol produces ester.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Draw radial array of soap molecules around central oil droplet with ionic heads outward in water.
diagrams_figures_and_maps.structural_or_conceptual_explanation: Hydrophobic tail interacts with grease/oil; hydrophilic ionic head interacts with water.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: A series of organic compounds having the same functional group, similar chemical properties, and differing adjacent members by a -CH2- unit (14 u mass difference).

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.si_unit_or_notation: Ethanoic acid + Ethanol -> Ethyl ethanoate (sweet smelling ester) + Water
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Used in synthetic flavors and perfumes.

textbook_exercises.question: Ethane, with the molecular formula C2H6 has how many covalent bonds?
textbook_exercises.answer: Ethane has 1 C-C single bond and 6 C-H single bonds, giving a total of 7 covalent bonds. Option (b) is correct.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: Butanone is a four-carbon compound with which functional group?

short_answer_questions.question: Explain structural isomerism with isomers of butane.
short_answer_questions.answer: Structural isomers are compounds with identical molecular formula but different structural arrangements. Butane (C4H10) has 2 isomers: n-butane (CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3) and isobutane / 2-methylpropane (CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3).

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: What type of reaction is hydrogenation and why is it industrially important?
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Addition reaction. It converts unsaturated fatty acid oils into saturated fats (vanaspati ghee).

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Explain the chemical mechanism of cleansing action of soaps and why soaps fail in hard water.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Soap molecules have hydrophilic heads (-COONa) and hydrophobic tails (hydrocarbon). Tails dissolve in oily dirt while heads stay in water, forming spherical micelles. On rinsing, dirt trapped in micelles washes away. In hard water (Ca2+/Mg2+ ions), soap forms insoluble white precipitate (scum), wasting soap. Synthetic detergents do not form scum.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Compound X reacts with Na metal producing hydrogen gas. X oxidises with alkaline KMnO4 to compound Y, which turns blue litmus red.

qa.question: Identify X and Y and write the oxidation equation.
qa.answer: X is Ethanol (C2H5OH). Y is Ethanoic acid (CH3COOH). Equation: C2H5OH --(Alk. KMnO4 + Heat)--> CH3COOH.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Confusing structural formula of aldehydes (-CHO) with alcohols (-OH).
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Ensure double bonded oxygen on terminal carbon is drawn for aldehydes (-CH=O).
